Chapter 9: The Ongoing Work of Forgiveness and Letting Go.
You know, forgiveness isn’t usually something you do just once and then check off your list. For so many of us, it’s an ongoing process—especially if your life’s been shaped by old hurts or tangled relationships.
There are days when forgiving feels within reach, isn’t there? When the past seems a little further away, and time has softened the sting. But then, suddenly, something brings it all back—a call from a family member, a random run-in at the grocery store, or even just a memory sparked by a familiar place. Suddenly, the old pain flares up, and letting go feels so much harder than holding on.
Here’s something to remember: forgiveness isn’t about erasing what happened, or pretending it didn’t hurt. It’s about making the choice—sometimes over and over—to loosen the grip that anger and pain have on your heart.
There will be setbacks. Maybe words are spoken in the heat of the moment, or misunderstandings open up wounds you thought had healed. You might even feel regret. But alongside all that, there’s progress—a little more empathy, a growing sense of compassion. You start to realize that everyone’s carrying their own struggles and scars.
One evening, after a tough conversation, it finally clicks: forgiveness is as much a gift to yourself as it is to anyone else. It creates room for healing. It’s a way of saying, “I won’t let my past decide my future.” And honestly, most people never realize just how much freedom is possible, until they start letting go.
The journey of forgiveness isn’t finished—far from it. But you’re on your way. Every small step—a gentle word, a moment of really listening, a choice to move forward—becomes part of the tapestry of your life, slowly and patiently being untangled.
